findings.title: Recursive remediation rejects compiler-produced Markdown lists
findings.observation: The response schema defines each Markdown list item as SafeInlineToken[], while the production compiler and canonical TypeScript model define each item as SafeMarkdownBlock[].
findings.trigger: A valid submitted report contains an ordinary or nested Markdown list and a client reads the current or revision response.
findings.impact: The report persists successfully, but registered response serialization rejects the compiler-produced render model and can return HTTP 500; generated OpenAPI advertises the same incorrect shape.

evidence.description: The actual compiler output for '- one\n- two' fails SafeReportRenderModelSchema, and buildApp/app.inject returns 500 INTERNAL_ERROR when serializing it.
compileSafeMarkdown emits blockTokens for every list item and the canonical type is SafeMarkdownBlock[][], contrary to reports.ts lines 117-120.
The new passing test fabricates inline_code tokens as list items, a shape the production compiler never emits.

findings.remediation: Define a recursive SafeMarkdownBlock schema and use block references for list items, regenerate OpenAPI, and cover actual compiler output through schema validation and response serialization, including nested lists.
findings.verification: Compiler-produced ordinary/nested lists pass the registered schema and current/revision endpoints return 200 while unsafe nested tokens remain rejected; all contract, OpenAPI and full checks pass.

findings.impact: The exact old binary remains ready and can serve the previously accepted LP-01/LP-02 behavior.
